audits.title: SEC545: GenAI and LLM Application Security (GIAC GAIPS)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Partial 33%; N2 Partial 52%; N3 Weak 14%; N4 Weak 19%; N5 Weak 14%; N6 Weak 8%; N8 Weak 20%; N10 Weak 29%; N12 Partial 44%; R3.1 Partial 40%; R4.1 Weak 11%; R9.1 Weak 13%
audits.note: MCP/OAuth attack labs and authentication/authorisation topics support partial delegated-token and scope coverage. AI incident-investigation lab supports using an agent for own work. No bank lifecycle or recertification exercise evidenced.
audits.old_fit: Strong Expert-level option for N12 (agent/MCP security, supply chain, hosting, threat modelling) for AppSec and architecture staff, also deep on N5.4 attacks on the bank's AI; the draft R5.1 tag is not supported (no action tiers, enforcement point or stop mechanism).
audits.old_summary: N2 Expert 52% Partial; N12 Expert 44% Partial; R3.1 Expert 40% Partial; N1 Expert 33% Partial; N10 Expert 29% Weak; N8 Expert 20% Weak; N4 Expert 19% Weak; N3 Expert 14% Weak; N5 Expert 14% Weak

audits.title: SEC411: AI Security Principles and Practices: GenAI and LLM Defense
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N2 Partial 33%; N3 Partial 48%; N4 Weak 14%; N5 Weak 22%; N6 Weak 8%; N7 Weak 20%; N8 Weak 27%; N12 Partial 48%; R1.1 Weak 22%; R3.1 Partial 67%; R4.1 Weak 22%
audits.note: LLM Basics labs cover randomness, context windows and confabulation. MCP Lockdown lab includes description pinning, context isolation and approval. This does not demonstrate complete operator supervision or content-and-code hashing.
audits.old_fit: Good Practitioner-level defensive bridge into AI security (guardrails, MCP, injection IR) and a lighter, cheaper entry to N12 than SEC545; it also covers N5.4 well, but the draft N1 tag is not supported (it is about securing AI, not AI's uses in cyber).
audits.old_summary: R3.1 Practitioner 67% Partial; N12 Expert 48% Partial; N2 Practitioner 33% Partial; N5 Practitioner 22% Weak; R1.1 Practitioner 22% Weak; N3 Practitioner 19% Weak; N4 Practitioner 14% Weak

audits.title: SEC495: Leveraging LLMs — Building & Securing RAG, Contextual RAG and Agentic RAG
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N2 Partial 38%; N3 Weak 24%; N4 Weak 14%; N6 Weak 29%; N9 Weak 7%; N10 Weak 29%; N12 Weak 15%
audits.note: Provider syllabus teaches RAG prompting, attribution, ACLs and local-data handling through build labs. It does not map bank classifications or provide a complete evaluation suite.
audits.old_fit: Useful short hands-on primer for engineers starting on N10 (RAG, local hosting) with some N3 content, but it is an intro build course; the draft N3 tag is only partly supported and it does not teach agent supervision.
audits.old_summary: N2 Practitioner 38% Partial; N10 Expert 29% Weak; N3 Practitioner 24% Weak; N12 Expert 15% Weak; N4 Practitioner 14% Weak

audits.title: SEC535: Offensive AI — Attack Tools and Techniques (GIAC GOAA)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Partial 56%; N2 Partial 38%; N3 Weak 5%; N5 Partial 61%; N6 Weak 17%; N10 Weak 12%
audits.note: SEC535 outline includes model capabilities, decision loops, custom assistants and multimodal deepfakes. Anomalous model behaviour is mentioned; safe agent operation is not the course's purpose.
audits.old_fit: Best hands-on option in this batch for N5 (AI-enabled phishing, deepfakes, malware) for red teams and threat intel; the draft R3.2 tag is not supported (no containment or validation of self-directed testing agents).
audits.old_summary: N5 Practitioner 61% Partial; N1 Practitioner 56% Partial; N6 Practitioner 17% Weak

audits.title: SEC536: Adversarial AI — Penetration Testing AI Systems (GIAC GAIPT)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N2 Partial 48%; N3 Weak 29%; N4 Weak 14%; N5 Weak 17%; N8 Weak 13%; N12 Partial 44%; R3.1 Strong 73%
audits.note: SEC536 explains model internals and the AI application stack, with agent/MCP attack surfaces. Supply-chain attacks support risk knowledge, not a complete safe-connector operating process.
audits.old_fit: Primary option for R3.1 (red-teaming the bank's agents) with labs on agent, multi-agent and MCP attacks, and it covers N5.4 in depth; gaps are the named red-team guides (OWASP GenAI, CSA agentic) and automated red-team programmes.
audits.old_summary: R3.1 Expert 73% Strong; N12 Expert 44% Partial; N3 Practitioner 29% Weak; N5 Practitioner 17% Weak

audits.title: SEC537: AI for Offensive Security (SEC535 + SEC536 bundle)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Partial 56%; N2 Partial 57%; N3 Weak 29%; N4 Weak 14%; N5 Strong 78%; N6 Weak 17%; N8 Weak 13%; N10 Weak 12%; N12 Partial 44%; R3.1 Strong 73%
audits.note: Bundle comprises SEC535 and SEC536. Supplemental coverage follows their published component syllabi; overlapping content is not additive.
audits.old_fit: Duplicate of SEC535 + SEC536; choose it only for offensive staff who need both R3.1 and N5 hands-on, otherwise buy the single course that matches the role.
audits.old_summary: N5 Practitioner 78% Strong; R3.1 Expert 73% Strong; N1 Practitioner 56% Partial; N12 Expert 44% Partial; N3 Practitioner 29% Weak; N6 Practitioner 17% Weak

audits.title: SEC598: AI and Security Automation for Red, Blue and Purple Teams (GIAC GASAE)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Strong 78%; N2 Weak 29%; N5 Weak 22%; N6 Weak 21%; N7 Weak 13%; N9 Weak 7%; N10 Weak 29%; N14 Weak 14%
audits.note: SOAR workflow design, automation priorities and AI-assisted detection testing support workflow redesign and verification, but not full supervision of an agent or a domain evaluation system.
audits.old_fit: Good Practitioner option for SOC and purple-team engineers on N1 (AI in detection and response) and early N10 agent building, but the draft R1.1 tag is not supported: nothing on incidents where the agent is wrong, stopped or compromised.
audits.old_summary: N1 Practitioner 78% Strong; N10 Expert 29% Weak; N2 Practitioner 29% Weak; N5 Practitioner 22% Weak; N6 Practitioner 21% Weak

audits.title: AI Security Automation Engineer (GASAE)
audits.basis: Exam objectives only — no taught course credit
audits.summary: No taught coverage evidenced
audits.note: Teaching-coverage correction: this record is an exam or credential, with optional preparation sold separately. Exam objectives demonstrate assessment scope, not taught coverage. V7 objective-based scores are preserved in the Prior score column; they are not counted as course teaching. Select a separately assessed preparation course when planning learning.
audits.old_fit: Assessment only, not training: useful as the proof step after SEC598 (TR-007) for N1, but it adds no teaching; the draft R1.1 tag is not supported and R2.1 is not a need in rubric rev 289.
audits.old_summary: N1 Practitioner 44% Partial; N2 Practitioner 19% Weak

audits.title: SEC573: AI-Powered Security Automation — Python, LLMs and MCP (GIAC GPYC)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Partial 33%; N2 Weak 29%; N3 Weak 19%; N6 Weak 29%; N8 Weak 7%; N10 Partial 33%; N12 Weak 7%; R3.1 Partial 33%
audits.note: MCP build/integration labs introduce connectors; data analysis to minimise context windows teaches a model limitation. No scope-vetting or Skills-governance method evidenced.
audits.old_fit: Good hands-on route for engineers into N10 (building agents and MCP servers) with some N6 practice; it is a Python course first, the draft R2.2 tag is not a need in rubric rev 289, and it does not teach agent supervision.
audits.old_summary: N1 Practitioner 33% Partial; N10 Expert 33% Partial; R3.1 Practitioner 33% Partial; N6 Practitioner 29% Weak; N2 Practitioner 29% Weak; N3 Practitioner 10% Weak; N12 Expert 7% Weak

audits.title: SEC595: Applied Data Science and AI/ML for Cybersecurity (GIAC GMLE)
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Weak 22%; N2 Weak 5%; N9 Weak 13%; N11 Weak 17%
audits.note: Classical ML cybersecurity use cases genuinely contribute to N1, whose wording includes AI generally. Statistical testing/evaluation topics are transferable introductions only; they do not establish agent evaluation competence.
audits.old_fit: Off-topic for the agentic-era plan: classical ML for detection; N1.1 is touched only through ML anomaly detection (would score 1), and the draft R2.2 tag is not a need in rubric rev 289.
audits.old_summary: No need met at 2 or above

audits.title: SEC543: AI-Assisted Source Code Analysis and Exploitation for Pen Testers
audits.basis: Public provider/source desk review — syllabus evidence, not course completion
audits.summary: N1 Partial 33%; N2 Weak 24%; N3 Partial 33%; N5 Weak 11%; N6 Partial 38%; N7 Partial 47%; N12 Weak 11%; R3.2 Weak 20%; R4.2 Partial 38%
audits.note: Current SEC543 syllabus explicitly adds sycophantic agreement, verification, secure credential/sandbox/log configuration and a multi-model consensus lab. Findings are reproduced and documented, but patched/unpatched validation and the full supervisory cycle are not evidenced.
audits.old_fit: Useful Practitioner option for testers and AppSec on N6 (working with coding agents, verification), with partial R3.2.4 (validating agent findings) and a partial start on R4.2, though it is a user-of-agents course rather than harness building and measurement; R4.2.6-4.2.7 are not covered.
